description: [Documentation] Create the DocumentCache reference folder index at `reference/document-cache/README.md`.
acceptance-criteria: `reference/document-cache/README.md` exists and explains that the folder contains durable DocumentCache implementation, operations, evidence, and qualification references.
The index links to `reference/document-cache/operations-runbook.md`, `reference/document-cache/cdc-inv-evidence.md`, and `reference/document-cache/performance-qualification.md`.
The index links back to the owning E18 design/story docs, the DMS-1428 CLI README, `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`, and `docs/RELATIONAL-BACKEND.md`.
The index clearly separates DMS-1317-owned DocumentCache references from E19 Kafka/CDC connector runbooks.
steps-to-verify: Manually confirm the linked files are intentionally created in `reference/document-cache/` rather than under `docs/`.

description: [Documentation] Create the DMS-1317 CDC-INV evidence matrix at `reference/document-cache/cdc-inv-evidence.md`, covering CDC-INV-01, CDC-INV-02, CDC-INV-03, CDC-INV-04, CDC-INV-05, CDC-INV-14, and CDC-INV-15.
acceptance-criteria: `reference/document-cache/cdc-inv-evidence.md` maps each in-scope CDC-INV contract to PostgreSQL evidence, SQL Server evidence, existing narrower-story tests, new DMS-1317 tests, and explicit exclusions.
The matrix uses concrete test identifiers and file paths rather than only prose descriptions.
The matrix marks DMS-1318 restamp coverage as conditional or blocked unless the restamp implementation has landed.
The matrix marks CDC-INV-06 through CDC-INV-13 as E19-owned except for runbook cross-links.
`reference/document-cache/README.md` links to the evidence matrix.
steps-to-verify: Manually confirm every matrix row has provider-specific evidence or an explicit gap/exclusion.

description: [Tests] Add automated validation for the DMS-1317 evidence matrix so referenced test files and documented CDC-INV rows cannot drift silently.
acceptance-criteria: A unit test verifies that every in-scope CDC-INV ID appears in `reference/document-cache/cdc-inv-evidence.md` exactly once or in a clearly documented provider row.
The test verifies that file paths referenced as test evidence exist in the repository.
The test verifies that E19 and DMS-1318 exclusions are explicitly labelled rather than omitted.
The test is narrow and does not require running provider integration databases.
steps-to-verify: Temporarily break one matrix test path locally and confirm the validation test fails before restoring it.

description: [Tests] Add shared completed-projection API integration tests for ordinary resources across PostgreSQL and SQL Server.
acceptance-criteria: A shared `DocumentCacheCompletedProjectionScenario` covers API POST, durable work enqueue, projector drain, cache row verification, cached GET/query, API PUT, stale-cache avoidance, API DELETE, cascade cleanup, and public 404 after delete.
Thin PostgreSQL and SQL Server wrappers execute the shared scenario through the existing API integration harness.
The scenario verifies caller-agnostic cached JSON and does not duplicate materializer fixture assertions already covered elsewhere.
The scenario records or exposes enough evidence for `reference/document-cache/cdc-inv-evidence.md` to reference it for CDC-INV-02, CDC-INV-03, CDC-INV-04, and CDC-INV-05.

description: [Tests] Add completed-projection API integration tests for descriptor create, update, cache serving, and delete behavior across PostgreSQL and SQL Server.
acceptance-criteria: The descriptor scenario creates and updates descriptor data through the supported public/API path.
The test drains projection work and verifies descriptor cache materialization and descriptor read acceleration.
Descriptor delete behavior does not leave stale cache or work rows.

The scenario reuses existing descriptor runtime support and references existing descriptor materializer/provider tests in `reference/document-cache/cdc-inv-evidence.md` instead of repeating all fixture-level assertions.

description: [Tests] Add public API coverage for disabled lifecycle and projector-stopped backlog behavior without gating canonical API routes.
acceptance-criteria: When lifecycle is `Disabled`, an API write commits canonical data but creates no `DocumentProjectionWork` row.
When lifecycle is `Disabled`, read acceleration bypasses cache and status reports the expected non-operational state.
When lifecycle is `Tracking` but projector dispatch is stopped or paused, API writes still commit and enqueue durable work.
Backlog status is visible while canonical API routing remains available and cached responses are not served until work drains.

description: [Tests] Add public API rollback coverage for forced DocumentCache enqueue failure across PostgreSQL and SQL Server.
acceptance-criteria: The test forces an enqueue failure through an existing provider fault hook or a narrowly scoped test-only setup.
A public API POST or PUT that cannot enqueue work rolls back completely.
The test verifies no canonical row, relationship row, work row, or cache row is committed after the failure.
The test covers both PostgreSQL and SQL Server or documents a provider-specific forcing limitation in `reference/document-cache/cdc-inv-evidence.md`.

description: [Tests] Add focused provider integration coverage for projector and direct-fill races using the shared DocumentCache writer contract.
acceptance-criteria: The test creates current durable work with missing or stale cache for one document.
A direct-fill path and a projector item process the same document concurrently under real provider state.
Exactly one path commits the cache write or work acknowledgement, while the other observes an already-current or race-lost outcome.
Public reads remain correct after the race and the final work/cache state is consistent.

description: [Tests] Add provider integration coverage for candidate-independent S = C = W acknowledgement in the presence of a stale materializer candidate.
acceptance-criteria: The test creates a stale materializer candidate and then makes source, cache, and work versions equal and current.
The writer acknowledges the equal-version work without writing stale JSON.
Telemetry and result classification identify the already-current acknowledgement path.
Both PostgreSQL and SQL Server have equivalent coverage or a documented provider-specific reason for different assertions.

description: [Tests] Add provider integration coverage for blocked work mismatches and scrub or rebuild-page repair.
acceptance-criteria: The test creates a non-cache-ahead work mismatch under real provider state.
The projector leaves the mismatch pending and does not set the cache-ahead latch.
Explicit scrub or rebuild-page repair fixes the work relationship without changing cache incorrectly.
The behavior is covered for PostgreSQL and SQL Server and referenced from `reference/document-cache/cdc-inv-evidence.md`.

description: [Tests] Add runbook-visible status coverage for DocumentCache crash windows and incomplete retryable administrative state.
acceptance-criteria: The tests use existing writer or administrative fault-injection hooks at meaningful transaction boundaries.
For each crash window, durable state is asserted as one of no mutation, complete cache/work acknowledgement, or incomplete retryable administrative mutation.
Public status or CLI-visible status exposes diagnostics that match the durable result.
The tests avoid adding broad new fault-injection mechanisms unless an existing hook cannot express the required window.

description: [Documentation] Create `reference/document-cache/operations-runbook.md` for DMS-1317 operational workflows and link it from existing DocumentCache documentation.
acceptance-criteria: The runbook documents status interpretation, persistent projection failure, poison remediation, enqueue-vs-processing availability, lifecycle mismatch, unsupported Resetting recovery, activation, deactivation, rebuild, scrub, cache-ahead recovery, SQL Server prerequisite failure correction, and required scrub after suspected restore or unsupported direct mutation.
The runbook uses the shipped `dms-document-cache` command names and confirmation tokens from DMS-1428.
The runbook links to owning design sections for contracts, recovery constraints, and deferrals rather than copying design text.
`reference/document-cache/README.md`, `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`, `docs/RELATIONAL-BACKEND.md`, and the DocumentCacheAdmin README link to the new runbook.
steps-to-verify: Manually confirm the runbook links point to existing design headings.

description: [Tests] Add unit-level runbook validation tests for `reference/document-cache/operations-runbook.md` command snippets, links, and secret-safe examples.
acceptance-criteria: The tests extract documented `dms-document-cache` command lines from the runbook and parse them against the real `System.CommandLine` surface.
The tests reject examples that include connection strings, passwords, client secrets, or unsupported direct command-line secret patterns.
The tests verify runbook markdown links and anchors resolve inside the repository or to the intended GitHub blob URLs.
The tests verify required remediation topics remain documented.
steps-to-verify: Temporarily add an invalid `dms-document-cache` example locally and confirm the runbook validation fails before restoring it.

description: [Tests] Add integration tests for DMS-1317 runbook workflows that are not already covered by DMS-1428 command-surface tests.
acceptance-criteria: The tests execute selected runbook workflows through the real `dms-document-cache` process against isolated PostgreSQL and SQL Server targets where practical.

The tests cover status-driven remediation branches, including enqueue-vs-processing availability, cache-ahead recovery routing, scrub admission/rejection, and SQL Server prerequisite correction while lifecycle is Disabled.
The tests assert shared lower-camel JSON contracts, stable exit codes, and durable state after each workflow.
The tests intentionally avoid duplicating DMS-1428 parser/README tests unless the runbook workflow adds new behavior.

description: [Tests and documentation] Add a repeatable DocumentCache scale qualification entrypoint plus `reference/document-cache/performance-qualification.md` thresholds and result artifact guidance for DMS-1317.
acceptance-criteria: The qualification defines provider-specific thresholds for baseline/rebuild completion time, database CPU/IO/log pressure, repeated queue DML or write amplification, status/oldest-work latency, canonical write overhead, queue growth/drain after outage, and same-document enqueue/ack lock waits.
CI-appropriate guards rely on bounded query-plan/statistics assertions rather than huge data volume.

`reference/document-cache/performance-qualification.md` documents the heavier local, scheduled, or release-validation run for representative row counts, including PostgreSQL WAL/vacuum/bloat and SQL Server log/ghost/index observations.
`reference/document-cache/performance-qualification.md` states that a durable-baseline-cursor Jira ticket must be created if restart-from-beginning exceeds the agreed limits.
`reference/document-cache/README.md` links to the performance qualification artifact.
steps-to-verify: Manually verify the qualification instructions include pass/fail thresholds before any measured-result placeholder.

description: [Documentation] Document the DMS-1318 restamp disposition for DMS-1317 and keep the evidence matrix honest about conditional coverage.
acceptance-criteria: `reference/document-cache/cdc-inv-evidence.md` and `reference/document-cache/operations-runbook.md` state whether restamp coverage is deferred to DMS-1318 or included because DMS-1318 has landed.
If DMS-1318 has not landed, DMS-1317 docs do not fabricate restamp tests or claim restamp coverage.

If DMS-1318 lands before DMS-1317 closes, follow-up test tasks are added for Tracking, Disabled, Resetting, Rebuilding, set-latch rejection, API validators, Change Query mirrors, cache reads, and status.
The runbook links to DMS-1318 or the owning restamp design section for operator guidance.
steps-to-verify: Manually confirm the matrix labels restamp as blocked, deferred, or implemented with matching evidence.
